title: SDR Receiver Uptime and Feed Health
dataSources: APRS packets (`aprs:packet`), WSPR spots (`wspr:spot`), satellite passes (`satpass:prediction`), NOAA APT captures (`noaa:apt`), meteor-scatter pings (`meteorscatter:ping`), SSTV images (`sstv:image`).
app: Software-defined radio and ham-radio stations — APRS igate, WSPR beacon, NOAA weather-satellite (APT) receiver, meteor-scatter monitor, and SSTV decoder — logging to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal (sourcetype=aprs:packet OR sourcetype=wspr:spot)
| stats latest(_time) as last_pkt by sourcetype
| eval mins_silent=round((now()-last_pkt)/60,0), stalled=if(mins_silent>20,1,0)
description: Confirms your always-on SDR feeds are still decoding, since a crashed dongle or software lock is easy to miss for days.
value: Unattended receivers fail silently; a heartbeat across your feeds catches a stalled decoder before you lose a week of spots.
implementation: Track the last packet time per SDR feed; alert when a feed goes quiet longer than expected.
visualization: Table of SDR feeds with minutes since last decode.
grandmaExplanation: It checks your always-on radio receivers are still working, so a crash does not go unnoticed for days.
